contracts/plugin_context.py:R6:PluginCon:
R6 fires on `except (ValueError, TypeError) as e:` wrapping `stable_hash(row)` in `record_validation_error`.

NOT A SILENT SWALLOW. The handler does not return, continue, or pass: it logs the error TYPE and then computes `row_id = repr_hash(row)[:16]`, so the quarantined row still gets an identity and still reaches `landscape.record_validation_error`. The audit row is written either way; only the hashing scheme degrades from canonical to repr-based.

WHY THAT DEGRADATION IS RIGHT HERE. `row` is a row that ALREADY failed source validation -- by construction it is malformed external data, and `contracts.hashing.stable_hash` raises exactly ValueError/TypeError on the shapes that cannot be canonicalised (NaN, Infinity, non-serializable objects). Those two types are the named failure vocabulary of the call, not a bare `except Exception`. Re-raising instead would mean a row that cannot be canonically hashed never gets quarantined and never appears in the audit trail at all -- the pipeline would lose the evidence that the bad row existed, which is the opposite of what a quarantine path is for.

WHY ONLY `type(e).__name__` IS LOGGED. `contracts.hashing` canonicalization errors embed `Got: {obj!r}` -- raw row content. Row data must stay in Landscape and must not cross an ordinary logging boundary (logging policy; elspeth-05a5727489). Logging `str(e)` here would be a data leak.

PROVENANCE. This site was already judged and signed (fp=465818f82e63144b). It re-surfaced only because lane C05 added `@observation_boundary` to this method for the Tier-3 R5 row-shape guard, which rotated the method's scope_fingerprint. The code inside the handler is unchanged by this lane; this is a re-approval, not a new exemption.

WHAT WOULD INVALIDATE THIS. If the handler stopped producing a fallback `row_id` (returning or swallowing instead), if the caught tuple widened beyond the documented raise vocabulary of `stable_hash`, or if `repr_hash` stopped being collision-resistant enough to identify a quarantined row, this would become a genuine swallow and must be re-judged.

That is the whole point -- artifact metadata is stored in the audit trail, and a mutable mapping could be changed after the descriptor was constructed, so the recorded evidence would no longer match what was attested. Accepting `Mapping` here would accept `dict` and silently reopen that hole.

TIER-1 INTEGRITY, CRASH ON ANOMALY. The guard raises `TypeError(f"{field_name} must be a frozen mapping, got ...")`. It is a construction-time invariant on ELSPETH-owned ArtifactDescriptor state, not a parse of external input, so a tier-3 boundary decorator would be a category error.

WHAT WOULD INVALIDATE THIS. If artifact metadata stopped being required to be deeply frozen, or if the freeze marker changed from `MappingProxyType` to an owned wrapper class, this site would need to move with it.

R5 fires on `isinstance(item, MappingProxyType)` inside the `for key, item in value.items()` loop of `_require_artifact_metadata`.

DISTINCT FROM THE GUARD ABOVE IT: that one REJECTS a non-frozen top level; this one is the RECURSION TEST that finds nested mappings and re-enters `_require_artifact_metadata(item, f"{field_name}[{key!r}]")` on them. It is the mechanism that makes the frozen-metadata invariant DEEP rather than shallow -- without it, `MappingProxyType({'a': {'b': 1}})` would pass while carrying a mutable inner dict, and the audit trail would hold metadata that can still be mutated after attestation.

Note the deliberate asymmetry: a non-mapping `item` (str, int, list) is simply not descended into and is accepted, so this arm cannot be replaced by a rejection. Positive-form `isinstance` selecting a recursion target on an owned frozen type is dispatch, not bug-hiding.

WHAT WOULD INVALIDATE THIS. If the deep-freeze invariant were enforced upstream (e.g. by `deep_freeze` at construction with a proof the recursion is unnecessary), or if nested sequences also had to be walked, this arm would have to change shape and be re-judged.

contracts/schema.py:R1:get_raw_producer_:
R1 fires on `column = options.get("column")` in `get_raw_producer_guaranteed_fields`.

WHY NOT A @trust_boundary. `options` IS Tier-3 raw plugin config, but this function is not a parse-or-reject boundary over it: it PROJECTS what a producer can be said to guarantee, and it raises only by propagation from `get_raw_schema_config`. Declaring it `non_raising=True` would be false (a malformed `schema:` block does raise through it), and declaring a raising invariant would misdescribe a function whose contract for THESE keys is 'absent means the heuristic does not apply'. So it is honestly J, not D.

WHY THE DEFAULTED READ IS RIGHT. The absent-key result is `None`, and `None` fails `is_valid_field_name(column)`, so the branch returns nothing and the caller falls through to `guaranteed` unchanged. Absence therefore CLAIMS LESS, never more. That is the safe polarity for this function: an over-claim here would tell DAG validation that a text source guarantees a field it does not actually emit, producing a false audit claim; an under-claim only loses a heuristic convenience.

NOTE ON `is_valid_field_name`. The comment above this line explains that the gate deliberately asks the same policy `TextSourceConfig._validate_column` uses rather than restating `isidentifier()`/`iskeyword()`, so the two cannot drift apart silently.

WHAT WOULD INVALIDATE THIS. If absence of `column` ever came to mean a DEFAULT column name rather than 'no claim', the fail-safe polarity would invert and this read would start fabricating a guarantee -- re-judge then. Same if `_TEXT_HEURISTIC_PLUGINS` were widened beyond the closed `{'text'}` set whose observed-mode output shape is deterministic.

R1 fires on `options.get("queries")` in the condition `plugin_name == _LLM_HEURISTIC_PLUGIN and options.get("queries") is None`.

THE ABSENT KEY IS THE SIGNAL, NOT A MISSING VALUE. This is a STRATEGY DISCRIMINATOR, and it is the only site of the three in this function where absence selects the branch rather than skipping it. At runtime, `queries is not None` is what selects the multi-query LLM strategy, whose emitted fields are query-PREFIXED; with no `queries` key the single-request strategy runs and emits the bare `<response_field>` / `_usage` / `_model` trio. So `.get(...) is None` here reproduces the runtime's own selection rule exactly, and reading it any other way would make the guarantee claim disagree with what the node actually emits. A `KeyError`-raising `options["queries"]` would be WRONG: for a single-request LLM node the key is legitimately absent, and crashing would break valid pipelines.

The comment on these lines records the ticket (elspeth-db98d3f660) and the reason the trio is UNIONed rather than substituted, matching the runtime augmentation in both the LLM source config rewrite and the single-query transform's `_output_schema_config`.

WHAT WOULD INVALIDATE THIS. If the runtime stopped keying multi-query on `queries is not None` (e.g. an explicit `strategy:` option, or treating `queries: []` as multi-query), this condition would silently claim the wrong field set and must be re-judged against the new selector. The parity pin is tests/unit/core/dag/test_llm_source_guarantees.py.

R1 fires on `response_field = options.get("response_field", _LLM_DEFAULT_RESPONSE_FIELD)` -- the one site in this function with an EXPLICIT default rather than an implicit `None`.

THE DEFAULT IS NOT INVENTED HERE; IT MIRRORS THE RUNTIME. `_LLM_DEFAULT_RESPONSE_FIELD` is `"llm_response"`, the same value the LLM plugins apply when the option is omitted. So when a pipeline author writes no `response_field`, the node really does emit `llm_response`, `llm_response_usage` and `llm_response_model`, and claiming that trio is accurate rather than fabricated. Substituting `None` instead (the no-default form R1 would prefer) would make this gate UNDER-claim for every LLM node that relies on the default -- the common case -- and DAG validation would then reject downstream nodes that correctly consume `llm_response`.

STILL FAIL-SAFE. The value is not trusted blindly: `is_valid_field_name(response_field)` gates the claim, so a non-str or non-identifier `response_field` yields no guarantee at all. As with the `column` arm, the comment records that this asks the same policy the runtime twin (`build_llm_source_output_schema_config`) gates on, rather than restating its clauses.

WHAT WOULD INVALIDATE THIS. If the plugins' own default for `response_field` changed and `_LLM_DEFAULT_RESPONSE_FIELD` did not move with it, this line would fabricate a guarantee for fields that are never emitted. That divergence is exactly what tests/unit/core/dag/test_llm_source_guarantees.py exists to catch; if that pin is ever removed, this site must be re-judged.
